source_text:
πενταπλάσιον (δηλαδὴ τοῦ
πρώτου) ναρδοστάχυος καλάμου τε ἀρωματικοῦ, πρὸς δὲ μήου, πυρέθρου, ἀλόης,
μύρτων, κόστου, κασίας, ζιγγιβέρεως, κροκομάγματος, ἔτι δὲ κρόκου, πετροσελίνου
κυμίνου τε Αἰθιοπικοῦ. Τούτων ἕκαστον κόπτεται ἄκρως καὶ ἀρωματικῷ σήθεται
κοσκίνῳ· κἀκ τούτου τρισὶ δακτύλοις ἀφελών, οἴνου τε καλλίστου ξέστῃ μίξας ἑνί,
καὶ ὀλίγιστον ἐλαίου προσλαβών, εἶτά τι μετρίως ἀνακόψας, ἔγχει κατὰ τῆς
εὐωνύμου ῥινὸς διὰ τοῦ κέρως ἡμιόνοις νωτοφόροις τε καὶ τοῖς ὑποζυγίοις τελείοις
μίξιν τὴν τελείαν, ἵπποις δὲ τῆς κράσεως τὸ ἥμισυ τριετέσι τε ἡμιόνοις ἢ διετέσι τῶν
ἄλλων κτηνῶν, καὶ ὑγιαίνουσι, καθ' ἕκαστον ἔτος, τρίς, ὅπερ ἂν εἴη τριῶν ἐφεξῆς
ἡμερῶν· καὶ νοσήσαντι δὲ τῷ ζῴῳ τὸ θανατήσιον ὁμοίως ἐπαρκέσει, τῆς λοιπῆς
ἐπιμελείας, ὥσπερ εἰκός, προσφερομένης αὐτοῖς τῆς ἐξ ἔθους· ἄλλα γὰρ κατὰ τῶν
μικροτέρων παθῶν, κατὰ τῶν ὀχληρῶν δὲ τὰ ἄλλα εὐπορεῖν ἀναγκαῖον. [Θεραπεία
βησσόντων ἵππων.] Ἵππῳ βήσσοντι θεραπεία φακὸς ἐπτισμένος, ἢν δίχα τῶν
ἐλύτρων ἄκρως ἀλέσας ἢ λειώσας ἅμα ὕδατι ποτίσῃς· μέτρον δὲ τοῦ ὀσπρίου ζῴῳ
παντὶ καθ' αὑτὸ ξέστου τέταρτον ἂν εἴη σύμμετρον. Πᾶν δὲ κτῆνος καμάτῳ ἔκλυτον
ἢ ὀρθοπνοίᾳ περιπετὲς οὕτως ἰάσαιο· φθεῖρας ἢ κόρεις οἴνῳ λελειωμένους πότιζε, ἢ
πίσσαν ἅμ' ἀλφίτοις τὴν ὑγράν. Τῶν δ' ἄλλων ἀλλαχόσε θεραπειῶν τοῖσδε τοῖς
συγγράμμασι σποράδην ἐγκειμένων οὐκ ἀπορήσεις.
pass_a_gloss: Fivefold (namely of the first) of spikenard and of aromatic calamus, and besides of meum, pyrethrum, aloe, myrtles, costus, cassia, ginger, saffron-paste, and still of saffron, of rock-parsley and of Ethiopian cumin. Each of these is-chopped finely and sieved with an aromatic sieve; and from this taking with three fingers, having-mixed with one xestes of finest wine, and having-taken-in very-little oil, then having-beaten it moderately, pour down the left nostril through the horn to pack-mules and to adult pack-animals the complete mix, but to horses half the mixture, and to three-year mules or two-year of the other beasts, and to the healthy, according-to each year, thrice, which would-be of three successive days; and to the animal that-has-fallen-sick the killing [disease] it will likewise suffice, the rest of the care, as is reasonable, being-brought to them from custom; for other things against the smaller affections, and against the troublesome the other things, it is necessary to-have-plenty. [Treatment of coughing horses.] For a coughing horse a treatment is hulled lentil, if having-ground or pounded it finely without the husks you give-it-to-drink with water; the measure of the pulse for every animal by itself would-be a fourth of a xestes, proportionate. Every beast slack from toil or fallen-into orthopnoea you would-heal thus: give-to-drink lice or bedbugs pounded in wine, or the wet pitch together with barley-meal. Of the other treatments lying scattered in these writings you will-not-be-in-want.
pass_b_english: Fivefold — namely of the first — of spikenard and of aromatic calamus, and besides of meum, pyrethrum, aloe, myrtles, costus, cassia, ginger, saffron-paste, and still of saffron, of rock-parsley, and of Ethiopian cumin. Each of these is chopped finely and sieved with an aromatic sieve. Taking from this with three fingers, mix with one xestes of the finest wine, take in very little oil, then beat it moderately, and pour down the left nostril through the horn: to pack-mules and to adult pack-animals the complete mix; to horses half the mixture; and to three-year mules or two-year of the other beasts. To the healthy, each year, three times, which would be three days running. To the animal that has fallen sick of the killing disease it will likewise suffice, the rest of the care, as is reasonable, being brought to them from custom. Other things are needed against the smaller affections, and other things against the troublesome.

Treatment of coughing horses. For a coughing horse a treatment is hulled lentil, if you grind or pound it finely without the husks and give it to drink with water. The measure of the pulse for every animal by itself would be a fourth of a xestes, a fair amount. Every beast slack from toil, or fallen into upright-breathing, you would heal thus: give it lice or bedbugs pounded in wine, or the wet pitch together with barley-meal. You will not want for the other treatments, which lie scattered in these writings.

choices.term: ἔγχει κατὰ τῆς εὐωνύμου ῥινὸς διὰ τοῦ κέρως
choices.english: pour down the left nostril through the horn
choices.why: κέρως is the dosing-horn; εὐωνύμου ῥινὸς is the left nostril of the beast, not a ritual 'unlucky nose'.
rejected: pour against the lucky nose through a horn-instrument

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
